edges.description: C5a-C5aR signaling exacerbates and amplifies cutaneous mast-cell degranulation.
LYN-, SYK-, and BTK-mediated signals induce mast-cell activation and degranulation.
MRGPRX2 activation raises cytosolic calcium and initiates degranulation signaling.
Mast-cell degranulation rapidly releases histamine, leukotrienes, and prostaglandins.
Released inflammatory mediators cause vasodilation and leakage of plasma in and below the skin.
Released histamine activates H1- and H4-receptor pathways on cutaneous sensory nerve endings.
Histaminergic signaling in cutaneous sensory nerve endings produces pruritus.
Superficial plasma leakage produces the edematous urticarial wheal.
Deeper swelling beneath the skin manifests as angioedema.
Allergen-specific IgE cross-linking activates the Fc epsilon RI signaling route.
